title: NTC 热敏电阻温度计：读数不走直线
summary: 10 kΩ 固定电阻 + 10 kΩ NTC 分压接到 ESP32 的 ADC。温度一步步升高，读数的变化却一步比一步小；固件用 B 值公式换算回温度。
concepts: NTC 热敏电阻 NTC thermistor
B 值方程 / Steinhart–Hart B-parameter equation
分压器灵敏度 divider sensitivity
description: ESP32 用 USB 供电。3V3 → R1（10 kΩ）→ 结点 VTEMP → NTC 热敏电阻 TH1（25 °C 时 10 kΩ，B = 3950）→ GND；VTEMP 接一个 ADC1 引脚（GPIO32–39），引脚设成模拟输入。温度在 0、25、50、80 °C 之间变化。

cards.title: 温度等步长，读数呢？
text: **ESP32** 的 **3V3** 接下方 + 轨，**GND** 接 − 轨。
搭一个分压器：+ 轨 → **`10 kΩ`** → 中点 → **NTC 热敏电阻** → GND。中点接 **GPIO32**，把它设成 **ADC**。
单击 NTC，在「属性」里把温度依次设成 **`0`**、**`25`**、**`50`**、**`80 °C`**，每次记下引脚列表里的 ADC 读数。
越热，读数变大还是变小？每升高一样多的度数，读数变得一样多吗？

cards.title: NTC：越热电阻越小，而且是指数地变
text: - NTC 的意思是**负温度系数**：越热，电阻越小。它不走直线：冷的时候掉得快，热了以后掉得慢。
![](fig:rt)
- 厂家用两个数描述它：25 °C 时的电阻 $R_{25}$ 和 B 值。温度 T 用开尔文（°C + 273.15）：
![](fig:div)
- 固定电阻选 $R_1 = R_{25}$：室温时两个电阻一样大，中点正好在电源的一半，那里最灵敏。

cards.title: 测三个温度，再像固件那样反算
text: - 电路就是刚才那个。点**「检查我的电路」**。
- 通过后，按题目把温度设成 0、25、80 °C，用万用表测中点对 GND。
- 最后一题像固件那样：从电压算出 NTC 的电阻，再用 B 值公式反算温度。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **NTC 按指数变，分压又不是直线**，所以固件不能用一条直线换算温度，要用 B 值公式（更准就用三参数的 Steinhart–Hart 公式）。
- 固定电阻 ≈ 你最关心的温度下的 $R_{NTC}$。测 3D 打印机热床那样的 100 °C 左右，就换成 1 kΩ 上下。
- 分压器的上端接 ADC 的参考电压（这里是 3V3）：3V3 漂一点，比例不变，结果也不变。
- 坑：电流会让 NTC 自己发热，读数偏高零点几度。引脚上并一个 100 nF 到 GND 能减小噪声；只用 ADC1（GPIO32–39）。

caption.text: 越热电阻越小。冷的一端曲线陡，热的一端曲线平：同样升高 10 °C，电阻的变化差很多。

i18n.en: Hotter means less resistance. The curve is steep at the cold end and flat at the hot end: the same 10 °C rise changes the resistance by very different amounts.

caption.text: R1 在上、NTC 在下，中点 VTEMP 接 ADC 引脚：越热 R_NTC 越小，V_T 越低。

i18n.en: R1 on top, the NTC below, the middle node VTEMP to the ADC pin: the hotter, the smaller R_NTC and the lower V_T.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the ESP32 (GPIO32 already set to ADC) and the bottom 3V3 and GND rails are wired. **Why**: powering the board is a repeated skill; the NTC divider is the lesson. **Your job**: R1 (10kΩ) from the 3V3 rail to column 24, the NTC from column 24 to GND, then column 24 to GPIO32 (j7).
en.title: An NTC thermometer: the readings don't follow a straight line
en.summary: A 10 kΩ resistor and a 10 kΩ NTC form a divider into an ESP32 ADC pin. The temperature rises in equal steps, but each step changes the reading less; firmware turns the reading back into a temperature with the B equation.
en.description: The ESP32 runs from USB. 3V3 → R1 (10 kΩ) → node VTEMP → NTC thermistor TH1 (10 kΩ at 25 °C, B = 3950) → GND; VTEMP goes to an ADC1 pin (GPIO32–39) set to analog input. The temperature changes between 0, 25, 50 and 80 °C.
compare: **Compare**: The point: **equal temperature steps do not give equal changes in the reading**. If the reading rises with temperature, check that the NTC is at the bottom (middle node → NTC → GND). The working:
**NTC model**: R(T) = R25 × exp[B × (1/T − 1/298.15 K)], T in kelvin. NTC = negative temperature coefficient: hotter means lower resistance.
**Divider output**: V = 3.3 × R_NTC / (R1 + R_NTC). With the NTC at the bottom, **hotter means lower voltage**:

**Nonlinearity**: 0→25 °C drops 1108 counts (about 44 counts/°C), 25→50 °C drops 965 (about 39 counts/°C), 50→80 °C only 620 (about 21 counts/°C). One count is about 0.025 °C near 25 °C but about 0.05 °C near 80 °C. A straight line cannot turn readings into temperature.

measurements.ask: 0 °C: multimeter on the ADC pin (VTEMP) to GND

measurements.explain: R_NTC = R1 = 10 kΩ, exactly half: 1.65 V. This is the most sensitive point.

measurements.ask: Compare the change per degree from your three readings: (V₀ − V₂₅)/25 and (V₂₅ − V₈₀)/55
measurements.explain: The NTC resistance changes exponentially and the divider is nonlinear too, so a straight line cannot turn readings into temperature. Near 80 °C one ADC count is about 0.05 °C; near 25 °C about 0.025 °C.
choices: the hotter, the smaller the change per °C: about 36 mV/°C from 0 to 25 °C, only about 23 mV/°C from 25 to 80 °C
the hotter, the larger the change per °C

measurements.ask: As firmware does, convert your 80 °C reading back to a temperature (°C): R_NTC = R1 × V / (3.3 − V), 1/T = 1/298.15 + ln(R_NTC / 10 kΩ) / 3950 with T in K, then subtract 273.15
measurements.explain: R_NTC ≈ 1.27 kΩ → ln(0.127) ≈ −2.06 → T ≈ 353 K = 80 °C. That is the B-parameter equation (a simplified Steinhart–Hart).

hints: Wire the board's 3V3 to the bottom + rail and a GND pin to the bottom − rail.
3V3 → 10 kΩ → middle node → NTC → GND; the middle node goes to GPIO32–39.
Set that pin to analog input (ADC) in the pin table.

cards.title: Equal temperature steps — and the readings?
text: Connect the **ESP32**'s **3V3** to the bottom + rail and **GND** to the − rail.
Build a divider: + rail → **`10 kΩ`** → middle node → **NTC thermistor** → GND. Wire the middle node to **GPIO32** and set it to **ADC**.
Click the NTC and, under Properties, set the temperature to **`0`**, **`25`**, **`50`** and **`80 °C`** in turn; each time note the ADC reading in the pin list.
Hotter: does the reading go up or down? Does every equal rise in temperature change the reading by the same amount?

cards.title: An NTC: hotter means less resistance, exponentially
text: - NTC means **negative temperature coefficient**: the hotter, the lower the resistance. Not along a straight line: it falls fast when cold and slowly when hot.
![](fig:rt)
- The maker describes it with two numbers: the resistance at 25 °C, $R_{25}$, and the B value. The temperature T is in kelvin (°C + 273.15):
![](fig:div)
- Choose the fixed resistor $R_1 = R_{25}$: at room temperature both are equal, the middle node sits at half the supply, and that is where the divider is most sensitive.

cards.title: Measure three temperatures, then work back like firmware
text: - The circuit is the one you just built. Press **Check my circuit**.
- Once it passes, set the temperature to 0, 25 and 80 °C as the questions ask and measure the middle node to GND.
- The last question does what firmware does: from the voltage, get the NTC's resistance, then the temperature from the B equation.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **An NTC changes exponentially and a divider is not a straight line either**, so firmware cannot convert with a straight line: it uses the B equation (or the three-term Steinhart–Hart equation for more accuracy).
- Fixed resistor ≈ $R_{NTC}$ at the temperature you care about most. For around 100 °C, like a 3D printer's heated bed, use about 1 kΩ.
- Feed the top of the divider from the ADC's reference (here 3V3): if 3V3 drifts a little, the ratio — and the result — stays the same.
- The catch: the current warms the NTC itself, so it reads a few tenths of a degree high. 100 nF from the pin to GND reduces noise; use ADC1 only (GPIO32–39).

compare: **对比**：重点看：**温度每次升高相同的度数，读数的变化却不一样**。越热读数反而越大时，检查 NTC 是不是接在了下面（中间结点 → NTC → GND）。计算过程：
**NTC 模型**：R(T) = R25 × exp[B × (1/T − 1/298.15 K)]，T 用开尔文。NTC = 负温度系数：越热电阻越小。
**分压结果**：V = 3.3 × R_NTC / (R1 + R_NTC)。NTC 在下，**越热电压越低**：
**非线性**：0→25 °C 读数降 1108（约 44 计数/°C），25→50 °C 降 965（约 39 计数/°C），50→80 °C 只降 620（约 21 计数/°C）。同一个“1 个计数”在 25 °C 附近约 0.025 °C，在 80 °C 附近约 0.05 °C。所以不能用一条直线把读数换成温度。

measurements.ask: 0 °C：万用表测 ADC 引脚（VTEMP）对 GND

measurements.explain: R_NTC = R1 = 10 kΩ，正好一半：1.65 V。这一点灵敏度最高。

choices: 越热，每升高 1 °C 电压变化越小：0→25 °C 约 36 mV/°C，25→80 °C 只有约 23 mV/°C
每升高 1 °C 电压变化都一样（线性）
越热，每升高 1 °C 电压变化越大
measurements.ask: 用你的三个读数比较每度的电压变化：(V₀ − V₂₅)/25 和 (V₂₅ − V₈₀)/55
measurements.explain: NTC 的电阻按指数变化，分压又是非线性的，所以不能用一条直线把读数换成温度。80 °C 附近一个 ADC 计数约 0.05 °C，25 °C 附近约 0.025 °C。

measurements.ask: 像固件那样，用你的 80 °C 读数反算温度（°C）：R_NTC = R1 × V / (3.3 − V)，1/T = 1/298.15 + ln(R_NTC / 10 kΩ) / 3950，T 单位 K，再减 273.15
measurements.explain: R_NTC ≈ 1.27 kΩ → ln(0.127) ≈ −2.06 → T ≈ 353 K = 80 °C。这就是 B 值公式（Steinhart–Hart 的简化版）。

hints: 先把开发板的 3V3 接到下方 + 轨、GND 接到下方 − 轨。
3V3 → 10 kΩ → 中点 → NTC → GND；中点接 GPIO32–39 之一。
在引脚表里把这个引脚设成“模拟输入 ADC”。
startNote: **半成品**：ESP32（GPIO32 已设成 ADC）、下方电源轨的 3V3 和 GND 已经接好。**为什么**：板子的供电是重复技能；这里要学的是 NTC 分压。**你要做**：R1（10kΩ）从 3V3 轨接到第 24 列，NTC 从第 24 列接到 GND，再把第 24 列接到 GPIO32（j7）。
